stories.headline: Hundreds of thousands march in France again; clashes in Paris
body: Authorities say 320,000 people marched across France on the third straight weekend of protests; organisers say nearly half a million.
Mostly young people are protesting the cost of living and the state of schools.
Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon after marches turned violent at the end.
stories.vc: Youth unrest adds pressure on France's budget, which bond markets are already nervous about.

stories.statLabel: years of war before this truce
stories.headline: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families in Ukraine
body: People evacuated from Russian-held Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday and met their families.
They travelled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus.
It was the biggest truce since Russia's full-scale invasion.
stories.vc: Successful humanitarian deals build the trust needed for wider ceasefire talks.

stories.headline: Turkey and Ukraine to work on a new Black Sea grain corridor
body: Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to stop attacking civilian ships in the Black Sea.
He and Zelenskyy agreed in Istanbul to work on a new grain corridor.
Rubio said interest is growing in a limited Black Sea ceasefire.
stories.vc: Safer Black Sea shipping would ease global grain prices, helping food importers.

stories.headline: DC and Virginia sue to stop Trump's triumphal arch
body: Washington DC and Virginia filed a joint lawsuit to block a large triumphal arch Trump wants built.
They call it 'flagrantly unlawful' and fear traffic disruption and lost historic views.
They want courts to act before construction begins.
stories.joke: Building an arch is easy. Getting past the lawyers is the hard part.
stories.vc: Fights over federal construction projects add legal risk for contractors bidding on them.

stories.headline: London police arrest 139 at Palestine Action ban protest
body: Police arrested 139 people at a London rally against the ban on Palestine Action.
The group is classed as a terrorist organisation under UK law.
The UK Supreme Court hears an appeal against the ban on Wednesday.
stories.vc: Protest and terrorism-law cases test the UK's legal limits on activism.

stories.headline: A historic Athens café closes as its rebel neighbourhood gentrifies
body: Mouria, a famous café in Athens' left-wing Exarchia district, couldn't renew its lease.
For 44 years owner Christos Vanas has opened it every day at 7am.
Writers, artists and radicals have gathered there for decades.
stories.joke: Gentrification: when the revolution gets priced out by flat whites.
stories.vc: Rising rents in cool neighbourhoods are a sign of tourism money reshaping European cities.

stories.headline: New-age tech stocks gain; Ather jumps 27% on first profit
body: 40 of 69 listed new-age tech stocks rose this week, led by Ather Energy's 26.8% jump after its first quarterly profit.
CarTrade fell 22.3% after weaker growth.
The group's combined value rose $8.62 billion to $160.94 billion.
stories.joke: Ather: one profitable quarter and suddenly everyone's a fan.
stories.vc: Investors are rewarding profits over growth, a clear signal for startups planning IPOs.

stories.headline: Indian startup funding dips 29% this week
body: Indian startups raised $130.2 million from 26 to 30 October, down 29.2% from the week before.
But 32 startups raised money, up from 17.
E-commerce led with nine deals worth $33.4 million.
stories.joke: More deals, smaller cheques. The festive season hit VCs too.
stories.vc: Lots of small rounds suggest early-stage investing is healthy even as big cheques stay scarce.

stories.headline: IPO-bound StockGro's profit jumps 3.3x
body: StockGro's parent made ₹113 crore profit in FY26, up from ₹34.6 crore.
Revenue doubled, almost all from subscription fees.
It filed confidentially for an IPO earlier this month.
stories.joke: Teaching people to trade turns out to be a better business than trading.
stories.vc: Profitable investing apps are lining up IPOs to ride India's retail investing boom.

stories.headline: Fraudsters posing as executives stole €3M from a Capillary unit
body: A KPMG audit found the €3.04 million fraud at Capillary's Czech subsidiary was an external payment scam.
Fraudsters likely impersonated a senior executive and an outside lawyer.
Capillary has recovered €450,000 so far.
stories.joke: 'Urgent wire transfer from the boss' strikes again.
stories.vc: Impersonation scams, now boosted by AI, are a rising cost for companies and a market for security startups.

stories.headline: HMT launches 'Kannadiga' watches for Karnataka Rajyotsava
body: HMT will launch a 'Kannadiga' watch collection with Kannada numerals and the Karnataka flag colours.
It comes in strap and chain versions, priced around ₹3,500–3,600.
The launch marks the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava on 1 November.
stories.joke: Finally, a watch that tells time in Kannada.
stories.vc: Heritage brands are finding new life in regional-pride products.

stories.headline: Karnataka's villages will shrink as cities grow, plan says
body: Karnataka's population may grow from 6.9 crore to 7.4–7.9 crore by 2047, a state plan says.
Its rural population is projected to fall from 3.6 crore to 2.4 crore.
The plan estimates ₹5 lakh crore in investment over 20 years.
stories.joke: Bengaluru traffic is about to get a lot more company.
stories.vc: Urban migration on this scale drives demand for housing, transport and city services.

stories.statLabel: years Applegate was told she had MS
stories.headline: Christina Applegate's MS reversal shows how women's symptoms get dismissed
body: Actor Christina Applegate says her neurologist now thinks she doesn't have MS after five years.
In a Guardian column, writer Shakira Hussein says her own MS symptoms were brushed off as common for 'women like you'.
She argues misdiagnosis of women is not rare.
stories.vc: Women's health research gaps lead to costly misdiagnoses, a growing focus for femtech investors.
